description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the number of examples and the minimum FDE (Final Displacement Error) over 20 predictions, denoted as minFDE₂₀ (↓), for two methods: an unnamed method represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line style, and a “Random” method represented by an orange line with circular markers and a solid line style. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” ranges from 0 to 8 with integer tick marks at each whole number. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (↓),” ranges from approximately 0.21 to 0.24, with major gridlines and tick labels at 0.21, 0.22, 0.23, and 0.24. The blue line starts at approximately 0.24 at 0 examples, drops sharply to about 0.21 at 1 example, then fluctuates slightly between 0.208 and 0.213 across 2 to 8 examples, showing minor peaks at 3 and 6 examples. The orange “Random” line begins at approximately 0.228 at 0 examples, dips to about 0.218 at 1 example, then remains relatively stable between 0.217 and 0.223 from 2 to 6 examples, before rising to about 0.225 at 8 examples. A legend in the upper right corner identifies the blue line (with a gray square placeholder) and the orange line labeled “Random.”
